answer: A vouching-web design resists Sybil floods: a new identity joins only when an existing member stakes collateral vouching for it, like a sparrow endorsed by its flock. If the newcomer misbehaves or duplicates appear, the voucher's stake is slashed. An attacker flashing a comet of fake accounts must recruit a voucher for every identity, so cost grows with each fake while profits stay flat. One genuine opal of reputation outweighs a thousand cheap counterfeits — the attack costs more than it earns.
